back: Sum of all values ÷ number of values (for a frequency table: Σfx ÷ Σf).
The middle value of the data when it is arranged in order; with an even number of values, the mean of the two middle values.
The mode is the most frequent value; the modal class is the class with the highest frequency in a grouped table.

front: When is the **median** better than the mean?
back: When there are extreme values (outliers) that would distort the mean.

front: Why is a mean from **grouped data** only an estimate?
back: Exact values are unknown, so class mid-points are used to represent each class.

front: What is the difference between a **percentage** change and a **percentage point** change?
back: A rise from 8% to 10% is 2 percentage points, but a 25% increase in the rate.
